claim: For the seven-exponential third-order commutator-free Magnus method (3.19) of Blanes, Iserles, and Macnamara, there exists a single bounded \(C^3\) time-dependent three-state Markov generator \(A(t)\) and initial state \(y(0)=e_1\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), the method's one-step output at step \(h_n=10^{-1}100^{-(n-1)}\) has third coordinate \(\widehat y_3(h_n)=[C-\exp(c s_n)-c\exp(-s_n)]/C<0\), where \(s_n=h_n^5/2\), \(C=2\sqrt3/3\), and \(c=C-1>0\). The exact ODE solution remains in the probability simplex, while \(\widehat y_3(h_n)=-c h_n^{10}/8+O(h_n^{15})\), so the positivity failure does not contradict third-order convergence.

integrity.proof_type: analytic construction with exact matrix-exponential formulas

scientific_limitations: The constructed negative coordinate is O(h_n^10), so its practical magnitude may be very small.
The result does not imply negativity for every smooth generator or every small step size.
The novelty assessment cannot exclude unindexed equivalent constructions.
title: A smooth three-state Markov witness for loss of positivity in a third-order Magnus integrator
